locked_story.headline: Deep learning mapped the world's glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020, people checked them, and ice-contact lakes grew by 3,567 (Nature Climate Change, Zhao et al., November 20th); in the study's open inventory Alaska's ice-contact lakes grew from 931 to 1,078 and from about 881 to 1,191 sq km, Vitus Lake at Bering Glacier the biggest gain; the lakes explain about 11 percent of lake-terminating glacier loss, climate and geometry far more
locked_story.note: Rejected 11-26 as regional only with no Alaska site, runner-up 11-27 with the paper unread. Today the abstract was read on nature.com and the authors' open Figshare inventory (doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.34332987) was tallied: it reproduces the paper's global count exactly (10,118 to 13,685, +3,567) and gives Alaska-specific counts, area and the lakes that grew most, which removes both objections. ML is load-bearing: deep learning drew the inventory, people refined it.

rungs.note: 4 researchers (energy/policy, science, fisheries/rural/health, defense/aviation/wildcard), about 80 WebSearch calls and many uncapped index WebFetches. All four called it a slow Thanksgiving week.

Covered in round one: ADN, Alaska Public, Alaska Beacon (403 on articles), KTOO, Alaska's News Source, News-Miner, Must Read Alaska, KYUK, KDLG, KUCB, KFSK, KMXT, Alaska Native News, UAF, UAA, AVO, USGS, NOAA Fisheries, phys.org, arXiv indexes.
Figshare inventory of the Nature Climate Change paper downloaded and tallied by region (Alaska RGI region).
